claims.text: The deformation, hardness, and strength of equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi in a simple solid-solution state are governed by nanoscale precipitate formation.
Nanoscale precipitates modify the dislocation glide mechanism in CoCrFeNiTi.
The starting alloy is Co20Cr20Fe20Ni20Ti20 in atomic percent.
The starting alloy is in a simple solid-solution state.
The alloy will be nanoindented with a Berkovich indenter at 25 °C and a strain rate of 0.01 s^-1.
TEM will be used after nanoindentation to characterize the microstructure.
The hypothesis applies under loading from 0 to 1000 MPa.
The nanoscale precipitates may form through spinodal decomposition.
Interactions between dislocations and nanoscale precipitates change deformation behavior.
Interactions between dislocations and nanoscale precipitates increase hardness by 15% relative to the starting alloy.
Interactions between dislocations and nanoscale precipitates increase compressive strength by 20% relative to the starting alloy.
Precipitate formation causes a decrease in plastic strain relative to the starting alloy.
The starting alloy has a hardness of 500 HV.
The starting alloy has a compressive strength of 800 MPa.
Composition and processing history may affect nanoscale precipitate formation and distribution.
Composition and processing history may affect deformation behavior, hardness, and strength.
The controlled comparison will test otherwise comparable CoCrFeNiTi specimens with and without nanoscale precipitates.
The hypothesis is falsified if hardness and compressive strength without precipitates are within 5% of the corresponding values with precipitates.

contradictions.description: The alloy is described as remaining in a simple solid-solution state while its behavior is simultaneously attributed to nanoscale precipitates; the relationship between a precipitate-containing state and the stipulated simple solid-solution state is not resolved.

The intervention specifies nanoindentation and subsequent TEM but does not specify any heat treatment or other processing route that would create the required precipitate-bearing and precipitate-free comparison states.
The stated intervention is performed only at 25 °C, whereas the hypothesis is claimed to apply through 600 °C; no high-temperature testing procedure is defined.
